The final diagnosis of IgG4-RD (with KS and lupus-like features) is correct. Proteinuria is listed as negative on urinalysis, so it is unsupported. Several salient findings (positive direct Coombs/hemolytic anemia, low hemoglobin, abnormal EEG, elevated creatinine, obsessive behavior) were missed.

extracted_hpo: mucosal scattered black spots on the lips
opus_rationale: The probands were diagnosed with Peutz–Jeghers Syndrome based on mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation and confirmed STK11 mutation. The extracted HPO terms (mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation, café au lait spots, oral/lip pigmented spots) are all supported by the text; the patients notably lacked intestinal polyps and other symptoms, so no salient phenotypes were missed.
The diagnosis of Hyaline fibromatosis syndrome (ANTXR2 mutations) is clearly stated and genetically confirmed. All extracted HPO terms are supported by the case descriptions of both patients.

The text explicitly diagnoses Gardner syndrome with FAP and desmoid tumor. Extracted HPO terms (colonic polyposis, desmoid tumor, abdominal pain, hydronephrosis, tubular adenoma) are all supported. Missed features include anemia (Hb 60 g/L), fatigue, and dyspnea on exertion.

The diagnosis of pure hereditary spastic paraplegia due to biallelic POLR3A variants is well supported. Most HPO terms are accurate; however 'adult onset' is contradicted—both patients reported symptom onset in the second decade of life (juvenile onset), though clinical evaluation occurred in adulthood.
